title: Advanced emergency braking systems (AEBS)
scope_summary: Approves vehicle types with regard to an on-board Advanced Emergency Braking System (AEBS) that avoids or mitigates rear-end in-lane collisions with a preceding vehicle and impacts with pedestrians. Applies to heavy vehicles of categories M2, M3, N2 and N3.
scope_quote: This Regulation applies to the approval of vehicles of Category M2, M3, N2 and N3 with regard to an on-board system to: (a) Avoid or mitigate the severity of a rear-end in lane collision with a preceding vehicle, (b) Avoid or mitigate the severity of an impact with a pedestrian.
applies_to_components: emergency braking demand to the service braking system
electronic control system of the AEBS (complex electronic control system per Annex 3)
relation_to_other_regulations: For M2 vehicles and M3/N2 vehicles with maximum mass ≤ 8 t equipped with hydraulic braking, Contracting Parties signatory to both UN R152 and R131 shall recognize approvals to either Regulation as equally valid (alternative to UN R152).
Refers to UN R152 (passenger car AEBS) as performance benchmark for pedestrian ambition.
Refers to UN R13-H (Appendix 2 to Annex 6, k-test method) and UN R13 (Appendix 2 to Annex 13, k-test method) for measuring peak braking coefficient.
Vehicle categories as defined in the Consolidated Resolution R.E.3 (ECE/TRANS/WP.29/78/Rev.6).
Current version corresponds to the 02 series of amendments; transitional provisions for the 02 series in paragraph 12.2.

defined_terms.label: Advanced Emergency Braking System
defined_terms.definition: A system which can automatically detect an imminent forward collision and activate the vehicle braking system to decelerate the vehicle with the purpose of avoiding or mitigating a collision.

defined_terms.label: Emergency Braking
defined_terms.definition: A braking demand emitted by the AEBS to the service braking system of the vehicle.

defined_terms.label: Collision Warning
defined_terms.definition: A warning emitted by the AEBS to the driver when the AEBS has detected an imminent forward collision.

defined_terms.term: Vehicle Type with Regard to its AEBS
defined_terms.label: Vehicle type
defined_terms.definition: A category of vehicles which do not differ in vehicle features significantly influencing AEBS performance or in the type and design of the AEBS.

defined_terms.label: Soft Target
defined_terms.definition: A target that will suffer minimum damage and cause minimum damage to the subject vehicle in the event of a collision.

defined_terms.label: Vehicle Target
defined_terms.definition: A target that represents a vehicle.

defined_terms.label: Pedestrian Target
defined_terms.definition: A soft target that represents a pedestrian.

defined_terms.label: Common Space
defined_terms.definition: An area on which two or more information functions (e.g. symbol) may be displayed, but not simultaneously.

defined_terms.label: Self-Check
defined_terms.definition: An integrated function that checks for a system failure on a continuous basis at least while the system is active.

defined_terms.label: Time To Collision
defined_terms.definition: Longitudinal distance between subject vehicle and target divided by their longitudinal relative speed, at any instant in time.

defined_terms.label: Initialisation
defined_terms.definition: The process of setting-up the operation of the system after switching ON the vehicle until it is fully functioning.

defined_terms.term: Mass of a vehicle in running order
defined_terms.label: Mass in running order
defined_terms.definition: Mass of the unladen vehicle with bodywork/coupling, fluids, at least 90% fuel, driver (75 kg), tools, spare wheel and, for buses, crew member if a crew seat exists.

defined_terms.label: Maximum mass
defined_terms.definition: The maximum mass stated by the vehicle manufacturer to be technically permissible.

defined_terms.label: Dry road affording good adhesion
defined_terms.definition: A road with sufficient nominal peak braking coefficient permitting a mean fully developed deceleration of at least 9 m/s2 or the vehicle's design maximum deceleration, whichever is lower.

defined_terms.label: The System (Annex 3)
defined_terms.definition: An electronic control system or complex electronic control system that provides or forms part of the control transmission of the AEBS function.

applicability_hints: Only applies to heavy vehicles M2, M3, N2, N3; passenger cars and light commercial vehicles (M1, N1) are covered by UN R152 instead.

A forward-looking radar, camera or lidar sensor used for collision detection and its control ECU are part of the AEBS and fall under the vehicle approval, including the Annex 3 complex electronic control system safety concept.

Brake system components (EBS, hydraulic/pneumatic modulators) receiving the AEBS braking demand are relevant via the Emergency Braking interface, while braking performance itself is governed by UN R13.
Instrument cluster/HMI displays, tell-tales, buzzers or haptic devices delivering collision or failure warnings fall under the warning provisions (5.1, 5.5).
Deactivation switches and menus for the AEBS are covered by paragraph 5.4.
Changes to vehicle features affecting AEBS performance (e.g. front-mounted equipment, bumper, sensor position, mass) may require extension of approval.
Light M2/M3/N2 vehicles ≤ 8 t with hydraulic brakes may be approved under UN R152 as an equally valid alternative.
Simulation toolchains used to replace physical dynamic tests are subject to Annex 4 validation requirements.
